newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow customs ban on transit cargo may shake market.
newsitem.headline: Moscow customs ban on transit cargo may shake market.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport were unchanged over the past month, but forwarders warned that a customs ban on transit cargo through Moscow starting on March 20 would lessen demand.

"We are waiting for a small shock after the ban will be imposed...Clients must seek alternative routes, avoiding Moscow. This is not easy to do," said Nikolai Belyayev, sales manager of EMS Garant Post.

Lilia Sirbu, Ikaros international cargo service's chief executive, said that after March 20 she expected even more red tape than ususual at Sheremetyevo, which is legendary for its mysterious rules and delays.
Belyayev said the State Customs Commettee did not explain details of new rules, but said he understood the ban would include cargo trucked into Moscow.
Even customs officials appeared confused by the latest rule changes. "That's the first I've heard of the rule," said Vladimir Yemelyanov, head of the customs' press department.
Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow, said that rules could change what have been stable rates over the past four weeks.
"We do not see any rates increasing soon, but the customs ban would change the situation at the market, which is stable now," he said.

Belyayev of EMS Garant Post, a forwarder for Air France, KLM and ANA Cargo, said the market over the past four weeks was more active than February, but rates were unchanged. But he predicted the market would fall because the customs ban could lessen demand for air shipments.
Sirbu said she hoped the customs ban would be soon be cancelled.
Peter Vins, president of Vinlund Air forwarder company, said Lufthansa had increased its rates from Moscow about eight percent.
"I do not think that it will shake the market because forwarders can find good rates with other carriers, including Delta Airlines for U.S. destinations and Iberia Airlines for Europe," he said.
He said Delta has began active cargo operations between Russia and the United States. "They offer very good rates for clients," Vins added.
Chris Lewis, Chapman Freeborn Russia's senior cargo manager, said Delta also cancelled a cargo fuel surcharge from March 13.
Boris Panchenko, a senior cargo manager at Eruslan company, said new customs rules would be more complicated for clients.
"Big firms will adopt to the new rules quickly. Others will have a lot of problems or...go out of business," he said.

Alexander Selyan, Atran-Aviatrans cargo carrier's commercial director, said that the market was stable over the last four weeks. "We do not plan to change our rates...but it depends on general economic situation in Russia," he said.

Vladimir Pavlov, a cargo manager at Soby, Aeroflot's cargo agent, said that export shipments increased in recent weeks. "We had a few new clients who ordered shipments to Asian destinations," he said.
Vins said that cargo turnover was very stable for U.S. destinations over the last four weeks, and Mordvinov said his company had a big cargo shipment to South Africa recently.
Lewis said that last Friday his company made five-tonne shipment to Los Angeles with Delta. "It was a fresh start to work with Delta," he added.
Sirbu said that it may be possible to increase deliveries from India and Dubai in the coming months.
--Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
